decidable_fragment_of_T_Pi.summary: T_Π = T_shape × T_device × T_phase combined via Tinelli-Zarba arrangement enumeration. The decidable fragment depends on which shape operations appear in the verification query.

QF_LIA_linear.description: Linear arithmetic over positive integers. Dim equalities, inequalities, broadcasting (element-wise max), matmul inner-dim matching. Reduces to QF_LIA (Presburger arithmetic).

QF_NIA_concrete_symbolic.description: Reshape with one concrete factor: e.g. 8 * head_dim. Substitute concrete value → linear constraint. Decidable in polynomial time.

QF_NIA_bounded_symbolic.description: Reshape with bounded symbolic factors: e.g. heads * head_dim where 1 ≤ heads ≤ 128. Decidable via bit-blasting to SAT. NP-hard via SUBSET-PRODUCT reduction (proven in Lean).

QF_NIA_unbounded_symbolic.description: Reshape with unbounded symbolic factors. Enters full QF_NIA, which is undecidable by Matiyasevich (1970) / Hilbert 10th problem. TensorGuard mitigates via timeout and concrete fallback.

combination_method.reason: T_device and T_phase are finite-domain, hence not stably infinite. Nelson-Oppen requires stable infinity, so Tinelli-Zarba extension is used. Arrangement count bounded by Stirling S(k, min(k,n)), polynomial for small k (shared vars) and n (domain size).

qf_nia_interaction_from_reshape.summary: Reshape multiplication d1·d2·...·dk = d1'·d2'·...·dk' introduces QF_NIA constraints. The decidability depends on whether factors are concrete, bounded-symbolic, or unbounded-symbolic.

cegar_termination_bound.description: The CEGAR loop in TensorGuard refines abstract shape predicates. The termination bound |E| is the number of distinct error categories (shape mismatches, device mismatches, phase errors). Each CEGAR iteration eliminates at least one spurious counterexample class.

relationship_to_decidability.P_fragment: Without reshape: combined theory is in P. CEGAR loop terminates in at most |E| iterations where |E| = number of distinct constraint violation types. Each iteration adds one predicate to the abstraction. Since |E| is bounded by O(ops * rank), termination is guaranteed.
relationship_to_decidability.NP_hard_fragment: With reshape: individual Z3 queries are NP-hard (SUBSET-PRODUCT). However, CEGAR |E| bound still applies for loop termination — the number of refinement steps is bounded by the finite number of predicate candidates. Each Z3 call may take exponential time in the worst case, but the number of calls is polynomial in |E|.
relationship_to_decidability.undecidable_fragment: With unbounded symbolic multiplication: individual Z3 queries may not terminate. TensorGuard mitigates this by: (1) timeout-based fallback to concrete evaluation, (2) restricting symbolic dims to bounded ranges in practice, (3) CEGAR loop still terminates if Z3 returns a definitive answer within the timeout.

cegar_termination_bound.termination_guarantee: CEGAR terminates in ≤ |E| iterations for the decidable fragments. For the NP-hard fragment (bounded reshape), each iteration is NP-hard but the number of iterations is polynomial. Total worst-case: O(|E| × 2^(b·log(b))) where b = max bit-width of bounded dims.
